sections.overview: eBird maps this bee-eater's breeding and non-breeding range across South and Southeast Asia.
sections.identification: Adults have a chestnut head, yellow throat and blue rump above a green body.
sections.habitat: It occupies open woodland, forest edges and orchards, often near water or earthen banks for nesting.
sections.diet: It catches flying insects, especially honeybees and wasps, but also ants, termites, dragonflies, butterflies and grasshoppers.
sections.behavior: It often watches from a perch before pursuing prey in the air; birds may gather at communal evening roosts.
sections.reproduction: Pairs excavate a burrow in a bank or similar earthen slope, nesting alone or in loose colonies; both parents incubate the eggs.
sections.ecology: The Blue-tailed Bee-eater is among its close relatives; BirdTree-based summaries estimate their divergence at about 5.1 million years, and its linked profile compares the pair.
sections.conservation: The cited bird account reports a global IUCN status of Least Concern; this category does not mean every local population is stable.
